dct_description_sm: The goal of this fieldwork was to establish a list of potential study sites to examine the reciprocal feedback mechanisms of ice-wedge change and vegetation growth in light of a warming climate. The landscapes of Axel Heiberg and Ellesmere Islands represent those of an extremely delicate polar desert and encompass an area that is predicted to experience the most rapid and greatest magnitude of effects of climate change. To this end, it is pertinent to examine the role that exists between ice-wedge sensitivity to thaw and their overlaying vegetation in order to project anticipated changes in high arctic ecosystem function and dynamics.
dct_title_s: Reconnaissance data on ice-wedges and polar vegetation of Axel Heiberg and Ellesmere Islands, Nunavut
